newsitem.title: USA: EMU budget forecasts need revision--Dini.
newsitem.headline: EMU budget forecasts need revision--Dini.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Monday that current forecasts on budget deficits of countries intending to take part in European monetary union are bound to be revised, and said that future economic prospects should also be taken into account.

"Forecasts are very uncertain and possible error is considerably larger than a tenth of a point, more on the order of half a point or even a full point," Dini said in a speech prepared for delivery to a conference here.
He was referring to the 3 percent deficit/GDP limit required to take part in EMU.

"Substantial revisions may be made between the publication of the preliminary estimates at the end of the year and the release of the final statistics that the European Council will consider in its evalutation in May 1998," Dini, who was formerly Prime Minister and Treasury Minister, warned.
"The European Council will inevitably have to consider trends and forecasts at least for 1998 in order to assess whether a country has achieved a lasting reduction in its deficit," he added.
Dini also warned that "it would be most undesirable for important decisions to be taken on the basis of data for 1997 that turned out to be very different in 1998 and the following years."
If a country with weak prospects were to be admitted and a country with solid prospects rejected, the political consequences would be adverse, he added.
